identity.question: Pedro Sánchez out as PM of Spain by December 31, 2026?

literal_rule: YES if Sánchez ceases to be PM at any time after creation and by 2026-12-31 23:59 ET. An earlier resignation/removal announcement resolves YES even if effective later; detention/effective removal/permanent prevention may qualify. Official government/person information is primary.

dated_facts.fact: La Moncloa’s 17:37Z Oct 19 agenda calls Sánchez Presidente del Gobierno and lists official events that day. A same-URL 19:35Z refresh returned 403; later public status is unknown.
RD 806/2026 dated Oct 5, published BOE Oct 6, dissolves the 2023-elected chambers and calls both-chamber elections for Sunday Nov 29, 2026. It sets no new Congress session or PM departure date.

Law 50/1997 Art.21: Government ceases after general elections, specified confidence loss, or President resignation/death; outgoing Government remains in functions until successor takes office, facilitates formation/transfer, and generally handles ordinary business. It calls the incumbent “President of the Government in functions” and limits some powers. This does not decide if caretaker status satisfies the market’s personal PM wording.

Constitution 68(6): new Congress must convene within 25 days of election (by Dec 24, calculated). Art.99: King consults and proposes a candidate; first investiture vote requires absolute majority, second follows in 48 hours and needs simple majority; if no candidate wins confidence within two months of first vote, Congress dissolves and elections are called. Art.101: Government resigns after general elections, but remains in power until successor takes office. No session/investiture date is set in the captured decree.

rule_application_boundary: Law describes Government cessation and caretaker continuation; it does not settle whether Sánchez as individual legally ceases being PM during caretaker status under this market wording.
coverage_limit: No personal resignation/removal announcement was established in these sources; no exhaustive government/BOE/Congress/court search. New agenda request returned 403.
